Model Y L Canyon Drive: Six-Seat Family SUV That Hugs Corners Like a Sports Car + FSD 14.3.7 from Topanga Beach to Santa Monica

This one felt different the second we left the pavement.

I took the brand-new Tesla Model Y L through the canyons of Woodland Hills and it completely rewired what I thought a six-seater family SUV could do. This is not a stretched Model Y that just gained a third row and lost its soul. 

The weight is planted, the balance is dialed, and it leans into turns with a confidence that feels closer to a two-door sports car than a three-row people mover.

We spent real time comparing the adaptive suspension modes. In Balanced it stays composed and connected. Flip it to Rear Comfort and the character shifts — the rear settles into a softer, more isolated ride while the front gets a touch more movement. Joe (the Prez) sat up front with me first, then moved to the second row and immediately felt the difference. For families, this is the feature that actually matters. 

You can keep the driver engaged while the people you care about in the back get the smoother ride. Absolute game-changer.

Then we handed the wheel to Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v14.3.7 and ran it from Topanga Beach all the way to Santa Monica. Smooth, confident, and still the clearest proof that Tesla’s software is in a different league. 

No other six-seat EV combines this level of performance, efficiency, and autonomy in one package.

Key numbers that make the Model Y L special:
•  True 2+2+2 six-seat layout with second-row captain’s chairs
•  Second and third rows fold completely flat
•  0-60 mph in 4.4 seconds — quicker than the Model Y Premium AWD
•  Class-leading 0.216 coefficient of drag for efficiency
•  Adaptive continuous damping with Balanced and Rear Comfort modes
•  Longer wheelbase that finally delivers usable third-row space without killing the driving dynamics

This is the family SUV that doesn’t force you to choose between space, comfort, and the way it drives. It feels unlike anything else I’ve driven in this segment.
